chunks: And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say regarding a man who sought a woman for something unlawful against herself, and she struck him with a stone and hit a fatal spot on him. He said: There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if she is brought before a just Imam, he would declare his blood without liability.

key_terms.أَهْدَرَ دَمَهُ: he would deem his blood without compensation or liability
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَدْلٍ: a just Imam or legitimate judicial authority
key_terms.عَلَى نَفْسِهَا حَرَاماً: for an unlawful violation against her person
key_terms.مَقْتَلًا: a fatal blow or lethal spot

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman kills an attacker while defending herself from unlawful assault?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who kills a man while defending herself from an unlawful sexual assault. It states that she bears no sin before Allah عزّ وجلّ, and that a just Imam would not impose liability for the attacker’s blood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5188 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say regarding a man who tried to force himself unlawfully upon a woman, and she struck him with a stone, causing his death.
Imam (as) said: "There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah (swt), the Majestic. And if she is brought before a just Imam, he will dismiss his (attackers') blood (declare it as wasted)."
